samples.summary: Notes store is never disposed, so the new `readOnly` dependency leaks a permanent Yorkie subscriber per role change
samples.evidence: `YorkieNoteStore`'s constructor calls `doc.subscribe(...)` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:143) and discards the returned unsubscriber; there is no `dispose()` on the class. The effect at notes-view.tsx:127 now lists `readOnly` in its deps (line 167) and constructs a fresh `YorkieNoteStore` on every re-run (line 135), but the cleanup (lines 150-155) only calls `editor.dispose()` and nulls `storeRef` — it never releases the store's subscription. The Yorkie document belongs to the enclosing `CollabDocumentProvider` and outlives the effect, so each `editor` -> `viewer` downgrade strands a live subscriber and the whole store it closes over. This is exactly the hazard the diff fixed for docs (`store.dispose()` added at docs-view.tsx:574, with `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` added for the purpose) and that slides already handled (slides-view.tsx:1216); notes was left out.

samples.summary: New `withUndoUnit` in the Hangul commit path opens an undo unit without the required preceding `saveSnapshot()`
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit`'s own contract (text-editor.ts:3862-3866) states "`saveSnapshot()` must be called before opening a unit, never inside one" because on `YorkieDocStore` it also flushes the pre-edit caret/selection into presence, which is what Yorkie records as the reverse of the change. The new unit at line 5932 (`applyHangulResult`, the `result.commit && hangulComposingText === ''` branch, i.e. a jamo that commits immediately over a selection) is opened with no `saveSnapshot()` anywhere above it — contrast the sibling branch at line 5946 which does call `this.saveSnapshot()`. Consequence: undoing a Hangul commit that replaced a selection restores the post-edit caret/selection rather than the pre-edit one. The new frontend test 'a Hangul commit over a select-all is one undo unit' only asserts unit count and text, so it does not catch this.
searchedFor: grep saveSnapshot call sites around withUndoUnit

samples.summary: `isRevokedShareLinkError` treats 401/403 from an unauthenticated endpoint as a fatal verdict, so an intermediary challenge evicts a live editing session
samples.evidence: `resolveShareLink` uses bare `fetch` with no credentials (share-links.ts:102), so the server itself never answers 401 for this route. But `isRevokedShareLinkError` returns true for every 4xx except 408/429, including 401 and 403. A reverse proxy / WAF / captive portal / SSO gateway that answers a background re-resolve with 401 or 403 makes `fatal` true in shared-document.tsx:1138, which unmounts the whole `YorkieProvider` subtree and discards anything not yet synced — precisely the failure mode the function's own doc comment says it exists to prevent. The function's stated intent ("the server's verdict on the link") is satisfied by 404/410 (and arguably 400); 401/403 are not verdicts this endpoint issues.
searchedFor: grep for resolve endpoint status handling in backend share-links controller

samples.summary: `requestLayoutRefresh` makes every batched edit measure its dirty blocks twice
samples.evidence: The wrapper installed at text-editor.ts:734 calls `requestLayoutRefresh()` for each held render, and `requestLayoutRefresh` (editor.ts:2615-2619) runs a full `recomputeLayout()` and then *restores* the pre-refresh `dirtyBlockIds` set. When the unit closes, `withUndoUnit` replays `requestRender()`, which runs `recomputeLayout()` again over that same restored set — so the blocks just measured are re-measured. Since every `withUndoUnit` body in this diff ends with `requestRender()` (handleInput:1047, handleEnter:2717, applyPastePlan:1568, handlePageBreak:2744, pastePlainTextFromClipboard:4301), this doubles the measure pass on the hottest path in the editor, one extra layout per keystroke. Not a wrong result, but a real cost the code comment does not account for.
searchedFor: read text-editor.ts requestRender wrapper (727-742) and withUndoUnit (3874-3885)
traced markDirty/invalidateLayout ordering in handleInput, handleEnter, applyPastePlan

samples.summary: `canUndo()` permanently discards the undo floor on a cap-sized stack whenever the mark cannot be located
samples.evidence: When `lastIndexOf(undoFloorMark)` returns -1 the code uses `stack.length >= YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH` (a hard-coded 50 that the SDK does not export) to decide the entry was shifted off the bottom, and latches `undoFloorMark = null; undoFloorDepth = 0`, after which `canUndo()` returns true unconditionally (line 3045). That test is not a discriminator: any other reason the mark goes missing — an SDK that rebuilds the entry in place, a history implementation that replaces the array, a future cap other than 50 — coincides with a full stack most of the time on an active document. The latch is irreversible, so a single false positive permanently removes the guard that stops a user undoing past the initial `setDocument()` load, which the surrounding comment says "would destroy blocks the cursor still references". The identity check at mark time (`undoFloorIdentityUsable`) only proves the accessor was identity-stable at that instant, not that the entry survives.
searchedFor: read the new tests in tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts

samples.summary: `writePageSetup` still writes through the raw `docStore`, bypassing the revocation the diff added for the same operation elsewhere
samples.evidence: The diff deliberately re-routed `guardedSetPageSetup` from `docStore` to `revocableStore` (editor.ts:3313) with the comment "writing to the raw store here would be the single page-setup-shaped hole left in a disposed handle". But `writePageSetup` (line 2307) — the other caller of `setPageSetup`, driven by `EditorAPI.setPageSetup` and by `ruler.onMarginChange` (line 2314) — still calls `docStore.setPageSetup(...)` directly and so is not covered by handle revocation at all. It is covered only by `neuterMutations(api)` replacing `api.setPageSetup`, which does nothing for a holder that destructured the method before disposal or for the ruler drag callback if it can still fire. Same inconsistency applies to `docStore.setDocStyles` / `updateStyleDefinition` / `resetStyle` / `resetAllStyles` at lines 3559/3604/3607/3610 and `docStore.applyStyles` at line 1379.
searchedFor: read writePageSetup (2299-2318) and the named-style api members (3546-3611)

samples.summary: The share-link query keeps polling every 60s after a fatal verdict renders the "Link unavailable" screen
samples.evidence: `useQuery` is called unconditionally at line 1120 with `refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`; the fatal branch at line 1140 returns an error view but the hook stays mounted, so a revoked link keeps issuing one request per minute per open tab for as long as the tab lives. Harmless but pointless traffic against the exact links the feature just concluded are dead.

searchedFor: grep 'this.saveSnapshot()|withUndoUnit(' in packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts (enumerated all 30 snapshot sites vs the 8 withUndoUnit sites)
finding.summary: The #1045 undo-cap data-loss shape is left unfixed on the other multi-block write actions (Tab / indent / outdent / format-painter / multi-block inline style)
finding.evidence:
`withUndoUnit` was added to typing, paste, Enter, page-break, Cmd+Shift+V and Hangul, but the remaining actions that write once per selected block are still unbatched:

- `handleTab` (text-editor.ts:2769-2781) — `saveSnapshot()` then `forEachBlockInSelection(... this.doc.setBlockType(...))`, one store write per list item.
- `handleIndent` (2814-2828) and `handleOutdent` (2835-2851) — same shape, `setBlockType` / `applyBlockStyle` per block.
- `pasteFormat` (543-546) — `saveSnapshot()` then `applyStyleToSelection`, which fans out per block.
- `Doc.applyInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:438-442) loops `visitRangeSlices` calling `this.store.applyStyle(...)` once per block slice; `EditorAPI.applyStyle`/`clearInlineFormatting` reach it via `applyStyleImpl` (editor.ts:1261). (Contrast `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl`, which uses the batched `applyStyles`.)

On `YorkieDocStore` each of those writes is its own `doc.update()` and therefore its own undo entry, and `withUndoUnit`'s own doc comment states the failure mode: the stack is capped at 50 (`YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH`) and `pushUndo` shifts the oldest entry off. Indenting, outdenting, Tab-ing, or bolding a select-all over ~100 paragraphs therefore still produces ~100 units, overflows the cap, and drops entries permanently — the same unrecoverable loss the change exists to remove, on paths a user reaches with one keystroke.

verdict.reason: The finding claims handleTab, handleIndent, handleOutdent, pasteFormat and the multi-block inline-style path are still unbatched, leaving the #1045 undo-cap data-loss shape. All five are batched in the working tree. handleTab wraps its per-list-item forEachBlockInSelection loop in withUndoUnit (text-editor.ts:2771-2785, with the comment "One write per selected list item, so one undo unit for the lot"). handleIndent (2819-2835) and handleOutdent (2843-2861) do exactly the same around their setBlockType/applyBlockStyle loops. pasteFormat (543-546) calls applyStyleToSelection, which wraps both doc.applyInlineStyleToCells (3598-3600) and doc.applyInlineStyle (3606-3608) in withUndoUnit; its doc comment at 3583-3587 names issue #1045 and the 50-entry cap as the reason. The keyboard B/I/U/S toggles (3565) and clear-formatting (3517) route through that same applyStyleToSelection. The EditorAPI side is covered too: applyStyleImpl uses doc.batch for both the cell-rectangle write (editor.ts:1260) and the ordinary range write (editor.ts:1267), with a comment at 1252-1257 citing the same #1045 cap; clearInlineFormatting (editor.ts:3444-3450) delegates to applyStyleImpl and inherits it. withUndoUnit (3874-3885) is doc.batch (model/document.ts:146-153 -> store.batch), and a store batch is one doc.update = one undo unit (pinned by yorkie-note-store.test.ts:61-78). The premise is false at every line range the finding cites, including the ones the reviewer says they read.

finding.summary: A transient share-link revalidation failure now tears down the live editing session
finding.evidence: `SharedDocumentByToken` was changed from a resolve-once `useEffect` to `useQuery({ refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS, refetchOnWindowFocus: true, staleTime: 0, retry: 1 })`, and the render guard is `if (!token || error || !resolved)`. In react-query a *background refetch* failure sets `error` while `data` is retained, so after two consecutive failures (retry: 1) the component renders the "Link unavailable" screen even though a perfectly good `resolved` is in hand. That unmounts `SharedDocumentInner`, and with it the Yorkie `DocumentProvider`, the docs/slides/notes view and the editor — mid-typing, on any 5xx or CORS/proxy blip from `/share-links/resolve`. The previous code could not do this: `resolved` was set once and never invalidated. The safe shape is to keep rendering while `data` exists and only evict on an authoritative negative (e.g. 401/404), i.e. gate on `error && !resolved` plus an explicit revoked/expired response.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is not in the repository. The render guard at shared-document.tsx:1138-1140 is `const fatal = error && (!resolved || isRevokedShareLinkError(error)); if (!token || fatal || !resolved)`, not `if (!token || error || !resolved)`. `retry` at line 1127-1128 is a predicate `(failureCount, err) => !isRevokedShareLinkError(err) && failureCount < 1`, not `retry: 1`. With a retained `resolved` and a transient error, `fatal` is false and `!resolved` is false, so SharedDocumentInner and the CollabDocumentProvider (lines 1072-1079) keep rendering — no teardown. isRevokedShareLinkError (share-links.ts:127-134) is true only for 4xx excluding 408/429, so 5xx, timeouts, rate limits and the fetch TypeError (CORS/proxy/offline blip) are explicitly non-fatal; share-links.test.ts:13-30 asserts that split. The remediation the reviewer prescribes ('gate on error && !resolved plus an explicit revoked/expired response') is already implemented verbatim, with a comment at lines 1110-1115 documenting the exact react-query data-retention hazard cited.
